question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Be like chalk and cheese
option_1: To be completely different from each other
option_2: To be very similar to each other
option_3: To have a close relation with another person
option_4: To be distantly related to each other
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be completely different from each other.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(to be) like chalk and cheese" is used for two persons or things that are utterly unlike each other, even though they may look similar at first glance. (एक-दूसरे से बिल्कुल भिन्न होना)

◦ Example: The two brothers are like chalk and cheese — one is a shy bookworm, the other a noisy sportsman.

• The image behind the idiom: chalk and cheese can look alike (both white, both crumbly blocks) but are completely different in nature and use — hence the sense of total dissimilarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To be very similar to each other" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning — it is the trap option for candidates who guess from the "look-alike" image.

• Option 3 "To have a close relation with another person" and Option 4 "To be distantly related to each other" wrongly interpret the idiom as being about kinship/relationship, whereas it is about difference in nature, character or quality.

NOTE

• Idioms with a similar sense of difference: "poles apart", "a world of difference", "different as night and day", "not in the same league".

• Idioms with the opposite sense (similarity): "two peas in a pod", "birds of a feather", "cut from the same cloth", "spitting image".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Everyone liked the lively music being played at the restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sombre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lively" (adjective) means full of life and energy; spirited, animated, cheerful. (जीवंत / उल्लासपूर्ण)

• "Sombre" means dark, gloomy, dull and serious in mood or colour — the exact antonym of lively. (उदास / गमगीन)

◦ Correct: Lively music raises the spirits, while sombre music creates a heavy, mournful mood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Durable" means long-lasting/hard-wearing — it is unrelated to mood or energy.

• Option 2 "Cheerful" (happy, bright) is a synonym of lively, not its antonym — a classic distractor.

• Option 3 "Speedy" means fast; speed is not the same as liveliness of spirit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lively: animated, vivacious, energetic, spirited, buoyant, sprightly, exuberant.

• Antonyms of lively: sombre, dull, lifeless, listless, lethargic, gloomy, subdued.

• Note the British spelling "sombre" (American: "somber").

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fourty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fourty" is misspelt. The correct spelling of the number 40 is "forty" — without the "u". (चालीस)

◦ Correct: There were forty students in the classroom.

• Remember the rule: four → fourteen (with u), but four → forty (no u). English keeps the "u" in four and fourteen but drops it in forty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Committee" (a group of people appointed for a function) is correctly spelt — it has a double m, double t and double e (CO-M-M-I-T-T-E-E).

• "Hypnotic" (inducing sleep or a trance-like state) is correctly spelt.

• "Tennessee" (a state of the USA) is correctly spelt — double n, double s, double e.

NOTE

• Other frequently misspelt number words: ninth (not "nineth"), ninety (not "ninty"), eighth (not "eightth"), twelfth (not "twelth").

• Commonly tested spellings in SSC: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, harass, maintenance, questionnaire, privilege, separate.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Raymond has opted the study of religion as his major subject in graduation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Theology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Theology" is the study of religion, God and religious belief. (धर्मशास्त्र / धर्म का अध्ययन)

◦ Correct: Raymond has opted theology as his major subject in graduation.

• Word roots: Greek theos = god + logia = study of ⇒ theology = study of God/religion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Psephology" is the study of elections and voting trends/statistics. (चुनाव विज्ञान)

• Option 2 "Philology" is the study of the history and development of languages, especially of literary texts. (भाषा-विज्ञान)

• Option 4 "Psychology" is the study of the human mind and behaviour. (मनोविज्ञान)

NOTE

• Other "-logy" one-word substitutes for SSC: Etymology (study of word origins), Entomology (study of insects), Ornithology (study of birds), Anthropology (study of human beings and societies), Numismatics (study of coins), Epigraphy (study of inscriptions), Seismology (study of earthquakes), Cardiology (study of the heart).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank.

Greta Thunberg _____________ when she dared to question about accountability with respect to global warming and climate change.
option_4: hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hit the nail on the head.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hit the nail on the head" means to describe or identify exactly what is causing a problem; to say precisely the right thing. (सटीक बात कहना / ठीक निशाने पर बात करना)

◦ Correct: Greta Thunberg hit the nail on the head when she dared to question about accountability with respect to global warming and climate change.

• The sentence praises her for raising precisely the right issue (accountability), so this idiom fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sow wild oats" means to lead a wild, pleasure-seeking life when young — irrelevant here.

• Option 2 "keep the pot boiling" means to keep something going/maintain interest, or to earn just enough to live — it does not convey accuracy of statement.

• Option 3 "give the devil his due" means to acknowledge the good qualities of a person one dislikes — it does not fit the context.

NOTE

• Idioms of precision/correctness: "hit the bull's eye", "hit the mark", "on the money", "spot on".

• Greta Thunberg is a Swedish climate activist who began the "Fridays for Future" school-strike movement — useful context for current-affairs based English passages.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

When Rajesh was going to college, he meet with an accident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. met.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subordinate clause "When Rajesh was going to college" is in the past continuous tense, which fixes the sentence in the past. The main clause must therefore take the simple past — "met" (meet – met – met).

◦ Correct: When Rajesh was going to college, he met with an accident.

• Rule: when a shorter action interrupts a longer ongoing past action, the longer action takes the past continuous and the interrupting action takes the simple past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has met" is the present perfect, which cannot be used with a clearly past time frame set by "was going".

• Option 2 "meets" is the simple present and clashes with the past context.

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because "he meet" is a plain subject-verb/tense error — the base form "meet" cannot stand as a finite past verb with the singular subject "he".

NOTE

• "Meet with an accident" is the standard Indian-English collocation for to have an accident.

• Similar structure: "While she was cooking, the phone rang." / "When I was walking home, it started to rain."

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

As soon as I shall win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shall win.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a clause of time introduced by conjunctions such as as soon as, when, till, until, before, after, by the time, the future tense is never used. The simple present is used instead to express future meaning.

◦ Incorrect: As soon as I shall win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.

◦ Correct: As soon as I win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.

• So the erroneous underlined part is "shall win", which should be "win".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "As soon as" is the correct conjunction for two closely following events — no error.

• Option 1 "hope" is a stative verb correctly used in the simple present in the main clause — no error.

• Option 4 "a Ferrari" correctly uses the article "a" before a consonant sound /f/ — no error.

NOTE

• The same rule applies to conditional clauses with "if": "If it rains (not will rain), we will cancel the match."

• Time/condition clause ⇒ present tense; main clause ⇒ future tense. Example: "I will call you when I reach home."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Some things are meant to be, and death is ______ for humans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. natural.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Natural" means existing in or caused by nature; normal and to be expected. The first half of the sentence — "Some things are meant to be" — expresses inevitability, so death being "natural" for humans is the logical completion. (स्वाभाविक / प्राकृतिक)

◦ Correct: Some things are meant to be, and death is natural for humans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "edible" means fit to be eaten — nonsensical here.

• Option 2 "spiral" means shaped like a coil (or a continuous downward movement) — it does not describe death for humans.

• Option 4 "viral" means caused by a virus, or spreading rapidly online — death in general is not viral.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with natural: natural death, natural resources, natural disaster, natural instinct, natural selection.

• Synonyms of natural (in this sense): normal, usual, inevitable, ordinary, expected. Antonyms: unnatural, artificial, abnormal.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

They complained that their manager was incompietent and knew nothing about the project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. incompetent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "incompietent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "incompetent", meaning not having the necessary skill or ability to do something successfully. (अक्षम / अयोग्य)

◦ Correct: They complained that their manager was incompetent and knew nothing about the project.

• Spelling key: IN + COM + PE + TENT — there is no letter "i" after "comp".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "incompitent" wrongly writes "i" in place of the second "e".

• Option 2 "incompeteant" wrongly inserts an extra "a".

• Option 3 "incomepetent" wrongly inserts an "e" after "incom".

NOTE

• Word family: competent (able, skilled) → competence/competency (noun) → incompetent (adjective) → incompetence (noun).

• The prefix "in-" here means "not" — as in inefficient, inadequate, incapable, inaccurate.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Distinguished
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dignified.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Distinguished" (adjective) means highly respected, eminent, of noble and impressive appearance or achievement. (प्रतिष्ठित / गरिमामय)

• "Dignified" means having or showing a composed, serious and worthy manner; commanding respect — the closest synonym. (गरिमापूर्ण)

◦ Example: The distinguished/dignified professor was honoured at the convocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mirrored" means reflected — it relates to reflection, not to eminence.

• Option 3 "Dramatic" means striking, theatrical or sudden — it describes effect, not respectability.

• Option 4 "Mediocre" means of only average or poor quality — this is an antonym of distinguished.

NOTE

• Synonyms of distinguished: eminent, illustrious, renowned, celebrated, esteemed, dignified, august, noted.

• Antonyms: mediocre, ordinary, undistinguished, unknown, obscure.

• Note the second sense of "distinguished" — the past participle of distinguish (to tell apart): "He distinguished between the two theories."

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Periodic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Irregular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Periodic" means occurring or recurring at regular intervals. (नियतकालिक / नियमित अंतराल पर होने वाला)

• "Irregular" means not occurring at even or regular intervals; uneven, erratic — the exact antonym of periodic. (अनियमित)

◦ Example: Periodic health check-ups are done at fixed intervals, whereas irregular visits follow no fixed pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Holistic" means dealing with the whole rather than the parts — unrelated to time intervals.

• Option 2 "Dynamic" means full of energy and constantly changing — it is not the opposite of "regular in occurrence".

• Option 4 "Tedious" means boring and tiresome — it describes quality, not frequency.

NOTE

• Synonyms of periodic: recurrent, cyclical, intermittent, regular, seasonal, sporadic (loosely).

• Antonyms: irregular, constant, continuous, unremitting, erratic.

• Related: the "Periodic Table" is so named because chemical properties recur at regular intervals of atomic number.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Manisha saw an old elephant / in the wildlife reserve / while she was / on safari tour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on safari tour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A singular countable noun ("tour") must be preceded by a determiner. The correct phrase is "on a safari tour" (or "on safari"), not "on safari tour".

◦ Incorrect: ... while she was on safari tour.

◦ Correct: ... while she was on a safari tour.

• So the segment containing the error is the fourth one, given as Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Manisha saw an old elephant" is correct — "an" is rightly used before the vowel sound in "old".

• "in the wildlife reserve" is correct — "the" is used for a particular, identified reserve.

• "while she was" correctly introduces a clause of time in the past.

NOTE

• Articles with singular countable nouns are compulsory: "He is a doctor", "She bought a car", "They went on a picnic/a trip/a tour."

• Note the fixed expressions without an article: "on safari", "on holiday", "at school", "in hospital" (British usage).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. more cheaper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "More cheaper" is a double comparative, which is always incorrect in English. The adjective "cheap" is a one-syllable word, so its comparative is formed by adding "-er" ⇒ "cheaper". Adding "more" as well is redundant.

◦ Incorrect: In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.

◦ Correct: In Nepal, the food is cheaper than in Sri Lanka.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "the food is" is correct — "food" is an uncountable noun taking a singular verb.

• "than in Sri Lanka" correctly completes the comparison.

• "In Nepal" is a correct prepositional phrase of place.

NOTE

• Rule of degrees: short adjectives take -er/-est (tall–taller–tallest; cheap–cheaper–cheapest); long adjectives take more/most (beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful).

• Never combine the two: "more better", "most easiest", "more worse" are all wrong.

• Adjectives with irregular degrees: good–better–best, bad–worse–worst, little–less–least, much/many–more–most.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. monologue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "monologue" is a long speech made by one person, or a person's inner speech/thinking to oneself. Someone "sitting alone, immersed in his own monologue" is absorbed in talking to himself or in his own train of thought. (स्वगत कथन / एकालाप)

◦ Correct: Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own monologue.

• Roots: Greek monos = one/single + logos = speech ⇒ speech by one person.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Synagogue" is a Jewish place of worship — it is a building, not something one can be immersed in as a thought.

• Option 3 "Mystagogue" is a teacher/initiator into mystical doctrines — a person, so it cannot be "his own".

• Option 4 "Prologue" is the introductory part of a play, book or speech — it does not fit a person sitting alone thinking.

NOTE

• Related literary terms: dialogue (conversation between two or more), soliloquy (a character speaking thoughts aloud, alone on stage — e.g. Hamlet's "To be, or not to be"), epilogue (concluding section), prologue (opening section).

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.

He has neither the policies nor the persanol charisma to inspire people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. personal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, the incorrectly spelt word is "persanol". Its correct spelling is "personal", meaning belonging to or affecting a particular person; individual. (व्यक्तिगत)

◦ Correct: He has neither the policies nor the personal charisma to inspire people.

• Spelling key: PER + SON + AL (from "person" + "-al").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three options are themselves misspellings of words that are already correct in the sentence:

◦ "cherisma" → the correct spelling is "charisma" (compelling personal charm), which is already correct in the sentence.

◦ "polecies" → the correct spelling is "policies", already correct in the sentence.

◦ "niether" → the correct spelling is "neither", already correct in the sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse personal (private, individual) with personnel (the staff/employees of an organisation): "Personal problems should not affect work" vs "The personnel department handles recruitment."

• The "neither ... nor" correlative pair used in the sentence is correct; remember "either ... or", "neither ... nor", "both ... and".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The judge wanted to hear straight from the horse’s mouth.
option_3: In close vicinity to the juror
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Directly from the person involved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means directly from the original, most reliable or authoritative source — i.e., from the person actually involved. (प्रत्यक्ष / विश्वसनीय स्रोत से)

◦ Correct: The judge wanted to hear straight from the horse's mouth — that is, from the person directly concerned, not through others.

• Origin: in horse racing, the most trustworthy tip about a horse would come from the horse itself; buyers also judge a horse's age by examining its teeth (its mouth).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Directly from the lawyer" is too narrow — the idiom is not about lawyers at all.

• Option 3 "In close vicinity to the juror" confuses the idiom with physical nearness.

• Option 4 "Having ears which never fail" is unrelated to the idea of a reliable source.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "first-hand information", "from the source", "get it straight".

• Opposite sense: "hearsay", "a little bird told me", "through the grapevine" (rumour/indirect information).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Virtual reality is the creation of a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "presented to our senses" is a reduced passive relative clause — it is short for "which is presented to our senses". The environment receives the action (it is presented), so the past participle (V3) "presented" is correct.

◦ Correct as printed: ... a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.

• The preposition "to" is right: something is presented to somebody/something.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "presenting to our senses" wrongly uses the present participle (V-ing), which would make the environment the doer of the action.

• Option 2 "presenting in our senses" is doubly wrong — wrong participle and wrong preposition ("in" instead of "to").

• Option 3 "presents to our senses" would create two finite verbs ("is" and "presents") in the same clause without a connector.

NOTE

• Reduced relative clauses: "the book (which was) written by Tagore", "the man (who was) injured in the crash" — use V3 for passive sense and V-ing for active sense: "the man standing at the gate".

• Note also the correct subjunctive "as if we were really there" (unreal comparison uses "were" for all subjects).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank.

Being a journalist, your first duty is to ____________ or else your colleagues might surpass you.
option_4: keep your ear to the ground
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. keep your ear to the ground.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "keep one's ear to the ground" means to stay well informed about what is happening; to be alert to news, trends and opinions. (हर हलचल की जानकारी रखना / सतर्क रहना)

◦ Correct: Being a journalist, your first duty is to keep your ear to the ground or else your colleagues might surpass you.

• This is exactly the duty of a journalist — to remain alert to developments, otherwise rivals will get the story first.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eat a humble pie" means to admit one's mistake and apologise humbly — it does not fit "first duty" of a journalist.

• Option 2 "have an axe to grind" means to have a private, selfish motive for doing something.

• Option 3 "build castles in the air" means to make impractical, day-dreaming plans.

NOTE

• Idioms of alertness/awareness: "keep one's eyes peeled/skinned", "keep tabs on", "be on the ball", "keep abreast of".

• The origin of "ear to the ground" is often traced to trackers/scouts who literally listened at the ground for approaching hoofbeats.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) He will come / (B) and receive you / (C) at the station / (D) when you will arrive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (D) "when you will arrive" contains the error. In a clause of time introduced by when, before, after, until, till, as soon as, the future tense is not used; the simple present conveys future meaning.

◦ Incorrect: He will come and receive you at the station when you will arrive.

◦ Correct: He will come and receive you at the station when you arrive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "He will come" is correct — the main clause rightly takes the future tense.

• Part (B) "and receive you" is correct — "receive" is correctly in the base form after "will come and".

• Part (C) "at the station" is a correct prepositional phrase ("at" is used for a specific point/place such as a station).

NOTE

• The same restriction applies to if-clauses (conditional type 1): "If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home." — never "if it will rain".

• Summary: subordinate clause of time/condition ⇒ present tense; main clause ⇒ future tense.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "good" takes the preposition "at" when it refers to skill or ability, not "in".

◦ Incorrect: She is very good in playing the guitar and singing songs.

◦ Correct: She is very good at playing the guitar and singing songs.

• So the erroneous segment is the second one, given as Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "She is very good" is correct — "very" properly modifies the adjective "good".

• "the guitar" is correct — names of musical instruments take the definite article "the" (play the guitar, the piano, the flute, the sitar).

• "and singing songs" is correct — the gerund "singing" is parallel with "playing".

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition combinations frequently tested in SSC: good at, bad at, expert in/at, proficient in, capable of, fond of, afraid of, interested in, jealous of, angry with (a person)/at (a thing), superior to, inferior to, married to.

• Note also: we say "play the guitar" (instrument) but "play _____ cricket" (game, no article).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. concern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "concern" (noun) means a matter of worry or anxiety; something that causes people to be troubled. (चिंता का विषय)

• The clause that follows — "as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems" — clearly signals worry, so pollution is a growing concern.

◦ Correct: Environmental pollution is a growing concern all around the world ...

• The collocation "a growing concern" is standard English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "interest" suggests curiosity or attraction, not risk or worry.

• Option 2 "duty" means an obligation — pollution is not an obligation.

• Option 4 "charge" means an accusation, a fee or responsibility — it does not fit "a growing ____ ... as it poses significant risks".

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "cause for concern", "a matter of grave concern", "growing concern", "of great concern".

• Synonyms of concern (worry): anxiety, apprehension, disquiet, unease, worry.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sources.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb that follows the blank is "vary" — a plural verb form. Therefore the subject must be plural: "The sources ... vary from natural causes ... to human actions."

◦ Correct: The sources of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions ...

• Meaning-wise, "sources" = the origins or causes from which pollution comes, which suits "vary from ... to ...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "source" is singular and would require "varies", not "vary" — subject-verb disagreement.

• Option 1 "sourcing" (the act of obtaining supplies) and Option 3 "sourced" (past participle) are not nouns that fit the slot after "The" and before "of environmental pollution vary".

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement rule: the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with the noun in the intervening prepositional phrase. Here the head noun is "sources" (plural), not "pollution".

• Example: "The causes of the accident are still unknown." / "The list of items is on the table."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. As a result.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "of these activities". Only "As a result" combines with "of" to form the fixed phrase "as a result of", meaning because of / as a consequence of. (के परिणामस्वरूप)

◦ Correct: As a result of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil ...

• The sentence states the consequence of the human activities listed in the previous sentence, so a cause-effect connector is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Since" (meaning "because") introduces a clause with a subject and verb, not a noun phrase — "Since these activities happen" would be needed.

• Option 2 "However" shows contrast, which breaks the logical flow.

• Option 4 "Therefore" is not followed by "of"; it is used as "Therefore, pollutants are released ..." — grammatically wrong before "of these activities".

NOTE

• Connectors of result: as a result of, because of, owing to, due to, on account of, consequently, hence, thus, therefore.

• Remember: "due to / owing to / because of / as a result of" are followed by a noun/noun phrase; "because / since / as" are followed by a clause.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists two similar causes of environmental pollution — (i) "human attitudes towards sustainability" and (ii) "their lack of environmental awareness". Two like items in a list are joined by the coordinating conjunction "and".

◦ Correct: One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability and their lack of environmental awareness.

• Note that both items are noun phrases, so only a coordinating conjunction can join them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "since" and 4 "because" are subordinating conjunctions of reason and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), not by the noun phrase "their lack of environmental awareness".

• Option 3 "but" shows contrast; the two causes here are complementary, not contrasting.

NOTE

• Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS): For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So — they join elements of equal grammatical rank.

• Keep parallel structure when using "and": "human attitudes ... and their lack of ..." — both noun phrases.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank must introduce examples of "individual choices". The preposition "like" means "such as" and can be directly followed by a noun/gerund: "choices like driving or using single-use plastics". (जैसे कि)

◦ Correct: Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices like driving or using single-use plastics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "example" and Option 4 "instance" are nouns; they would need supporting words — "for example" / "for instance" — and are normally set off by commas, so the bare noun cannot fill the slot.

• Option 2 "while" is a conjunction of time/contrast and would need a clause, giving no sense here.

NOTE

• "Like" and "such as" both introduce examples: "fruits like/such as mangoes and apples".

• Do not confuse this "like" (preposition = similar to / for example) with the verb "like" (to enjoy). After the preposition "like", a verb takes the -ing (gerund) form — "like driving", "like using".

question: Which of the following countries did India beat to win the Men's Hockey Junior Asia Cup 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India defeated Pakistan in the final of the Men's Hockey Junior Asia Cup 2023 to lift the title. The tournament was held at Salalah, Oman, and India won the final by 2–1. (जूनियर एशिया कप 2023 — भारत ने पाकिस्तान को हराया)

• This was India's fourth Men's Junior Asia Cup title.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hockey is played between two teams of 11 players each; a match consists of four quarters of 15 minutes.

• The world governing body is the International Hockey Federation (FIH), founded in 1924, headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland. Hockey India governs the sport in India.

• India's men's hockey team won 8 Olympic gold medals, and bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

NOTE

• Major hockey trophies/events: Olympic Games, FIH World Cup, FIH Pro League, Azlan Shah Cup, Asian Games, Asia Cup.

• Legendary Indian hockey players: Major Dhyan Chand (whose birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day), Balbir Singh Sr., Dhanraj Pillay.

question: In the realm of soil science, humus is considered:
solution_text:
The correct answer is decaying organic matter in soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In soil science, "humus" is the dark-coloured, decomposed (decaying) organic matter present in the soil, formed from dead plant and animal remains broken down by micro-organisms. (ह्यूमस — सड़ा-गला जैविक पदार्थ)

• Humus makes the soil fertile, improves its water-holding capacity, aeration and nutrient supply (N, P, K).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The process of formation of humus is called humification; the organisms that break down the litter are called decomposers (bacteria, fungi, earthworms).

• The topsoil (A-horizon) is the layer richest in humus, which gives it its dark colour.

• Soil is made of mineral matter (~45%), organic matter/humus (~5%), water (~25%) and air (~25%).

NOTE

• Soil types of India: Alluvial (most widespread, very fertile), Black/Regur (cotton soil, Deccan Trap), Red and Yellow, Laterite, Arid/Desert, Forest and Mountain, Peaty and Marshy (very rich in humus).

question: Which group of crops belong to fibre crops and are produced on a large scale in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jute and hemp.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jute and hemp" are fibre crops — crops grown for their fibre, which is used to make sacks, ropes, mats, carpets and coarse cloth. Both are produced on a large scale in India. (रेशेदार फसलें — जूट और सन)

• The four major fibre crops of India are cotton, jute, hemp and natural silk (the last obtained from silkworms).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jute is called the "golden fibre". It needs high temperature, heavy rainfall and well-drained alluvial soil; West Bengal is the largest producer, followed by Bihar and Assam.

• Option 1 "Gram and tur" are pulses (leguminous crops).

• Option 3 "Tea and coffee" are beverage/plantation crops.

• Option 4 "Wheat and rice" are food (cereal) crops.

NOTE

• Crop classification: Food crops (rice, wheat, millets, pulses), Cash/Commercial crops (sugarcane, cotton, jute, oilseeds), Plantation crops (tea, coffee, rubber, spices), Horticulture (fruits and vegetables).

question: Name the life-threatening disease caused by protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma that is transmitted to human hosts through the bite of infected tsetse flies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sleeping sickness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sleeping sickness" (African trypanosomiasis) is caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma brucei and is transmitted by the bite of the infected tsetse fly (genus Glossina), found in sub-Saharan Africa. (निद्रा रोग — सी-सी मक्खी)

• Symptoms include fever, headache, joint pain, and in the advanced stage, confusion, poor coordination and disturbance of the sleep cycle, which gives the disease its name.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Chagas disease" (American trypanosomiasis) is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi but is spread by triatomine ("kissing") bugs, not tsetse flies.

• Option 3 "Giardiasis" is caused by the protozoan Giardia lamblia and spreads through contaminated water/food.

• Option 4 "Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis)" is caused by Leishmania donovani and spread by the sandfly.

NOTE

• Other protozoan diseases: Malaria (Plasmodium, by female Anopheles mosquito), Amoebiasis/Amoebic dysentery (Entamoeba histolytica).

• Vector-borne diseases: Dengue and Chikungunya (Aedes), Filariasis (Culex), Plague (rat flea).

question: Who is an acclaimed Kathak dancer with many awards to his credit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Birju Maharaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938–2022) was the most acclaimed exponent of the Kathak classical dance form and the leading torchbearer of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" gharana. (पंडित बिरजू महाराज — कथक)

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1986), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and a National Film Award for choreography (for the film Vishwaroopam).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma — Santoor maestro.

• Option 2 Ustad Alla Rakha — Tabla maestro (father of Ustad Zakir Hussain).

• Option 4 Ustad Bismillah Khan — Shehnai maestro and a Bharat Ratna awardee (2001).

NOTE

• Kathak originated in North India (Uttar Pradesh) and is the only classical dance form with strong Persian/Mughal influence; its three gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• The eight classical dance forms recognised in India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: ‘Pinjar’ is a novel by ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amrita Pritam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pinjar" (meaning "The Skeleton", 1950) is a celebrated Punjabi novel by Amrita Pritam, set against the backdrop of the Partition of India (1947). It tells the story of Puro, a Hindu girl abducted during the communal violence. (पिंजर — अमृता प्रीतम)

• A National Award-winning Hindi film Pinjar (2003), directed by Chandraprakash Dwivedi, was based on this novel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amrita Pritam (1919–2005) was the first prominent woman Punjabi poet, novelist and essayist. She won the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956) for Sunehray, the Jnanpith Award (1981) for Kagaz Te Canvas, and the Padma Vibhushan (2004).

• Her most famous poem is "Aj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu", written on the horrors of Partition.

• Option 1 Kiran Desai — The Inheritance of Loss (Booker Prize 2006); Option 2 Kamala Das — My Story; Option 3 Anita Desai — Fire on the Mountain, Clear Light of Day.

NOTE

• The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour, instituted in 1961; the first recipient was G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam, 1965).

question: When was the Asian Games organised in India for the second time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1982.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the Asian Games for the second time in 1982, at New Delhi (the IX Asian Games, 19 November – 4 December 1982). The mascot was "Appu", an elephant. (1982 — नौवें एशियाई खेल, नई दिल्ली)

• India had hosted the first-ever Asian Games in 1951, also at New Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 1982 Asian Games was notable for being the first time colour television broadcasting began in India (Doordarshan).

• The Asian Games are held every four years and are governed by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA); the idea was promoted by Prof. G. D. Sondhi of India.

• Recent editions: 2018 – Jakarta/Palembang (Indonesia); 2022 (held in 2023) – Hangzhou, China, where India won a record 107 medals.

NOTE

• The motto of the Asian Games is "Ever Onward". The Games were first held at the National Stadium, New Delhi, in 1951 with 11 participating nations.

question: Who nominates members to the Rajya Sabha based on their excellence in literature, science, art and social service?
option_3: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is The President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service. (राष्ट्रपति — 12 मनोनीत सदस्य)

• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250 — 238 elected (representatives of States and UTs) + 12 nominated.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64); he/she presides over its sittings but does not nominate members.

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house — it is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, and a member's term is six years.

• The minimum age to be a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years (Lok Sabha: 25 years).

NOTE

• The President also nominates members to the Lok Sabha? — No; the earlier provision for nominating two Anglo-Indians (Article 331) was discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 (effective 25 January 2020).

question: Which Indian musician is associated with the Flute?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the world-renowned Indian musician associated with the Bansuri (bamboo flute). (पंडित हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया — बांसुरी)

• He has been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2000), the Padma Bhushan (1992) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. With Shivkumar Sharma he formed the composing duo "Shiv-Hari" for Hindi films such as Silsila, Chandni and Lamhe.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Ustad Zakir Hussain — Tabla; Option 4 Ustad Allahrakha — Tabla (Zakir Hussain's father).

• Option 3 Pandit Ravi Shankar — Sitar; he was a Bharat Ratna (1999) awardee and popularised Indian classical music worldwide.

NOTE

• Instrument–maestro pairs commonly asked in SSC: Sarod – Amjad Ali Khan; Santoor – Shivkumar Sharma; Shehnai – Bismillah Khan; Sarangi – Ram Narayan; Violin – L. Subramaniam; Mridangam – Palghat Mani Iyer; Veena – S. Balachander.

• Musical instruments are classified as Tat (string), Sushir (wind), Avanaddha (percussion/membrane) and Ghan (solid/idiophone); the flute is a Sushir Vadya.

question: The black soil area of the ________ is known as the Deccan Trap.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peninsular Plateau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The black soil (regur soil) region of the Peninsular Plateau is known as the "Deccan Trap". It was formed by the solidification of basaltic lava flows from volcanic eruptions about 66 million years ago (end of the Cretaceous). (दक्कन ट्रैप — प्रायद्वीपीय पठार)

• Black soil is also called "cotton soil" because it is ideal for growing cotton; it is clayey, retains moisture well and develops cracks in summer (self-ploughing).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Black soil is rich in iron, lime, magnesium, calcium, potash and alumina, but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter.

• It covers large parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

• The word "trap" is from the Swedish trappa meaning "step/stair", describing the step-like appearance of the lava plateau.

NOTE

• The Peninsular Plateau is India's oldest landmass, part of the ancient Gondwana; it is divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau, bounded by the Western and Eastern Ghats.

question: When did the British East India Company start the ‘permanent settlement system’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1793 CE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Permanent Settlement" (also called the Zamindari System or Istamrari Bandobast) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha (later extended to parts of northern Madras and Varanasi). (स्थायी बंदोबस्त — 1793, लॉर्ड कॉर्नवालिस)

• Under it, the zamindars were recognised as the owners of land and had to pay a fixed revenue permanently to the Company; 10/11 of the revenue collected went to the Company and 1/11 was kept by the zamindar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It was drafted with the help of John Shore. The "Sunset Law" provision meant that if a zamindar failed to deposit the revenue by sunset of the fixed day, his estate was auctioned.

• Other land revenue systems: the Ryotwari System (introduced by Thomas Munro and Captain Alexander Read, 1820, in Madras and Bombay — settlement directly with the cultivator/ryot) and the Mahalwari System (Holt Mackenzie, 1822, in the North-Western Provinces, Punjab — settlement with the village/mahal).

NOTE

• Lord Cornwallis is also known as the "Father of Civil Services in India" and for the Cornwallis Code (1793), which separated revenue and judicial administration.

question: The word ‘Swaraj’ was first used by Dadabhai Naoroji in the Congress session held in which place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dadabhai Naoroji first used the word "Swaraj" (self-rule) as the goal of the Indian National Congress in his presidential address at the Calcutta Session of the INC in 1906. (कलकत्ता अधिवेशन, 1906 — 'स्वराज')

• This session is famous for adopting the fourfold programme of Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education and Swaraj.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) is called the "Grand Old Man of India". He propounded the "Drain of Wealth" theory in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".

• He was the first Asian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892, Liberal Party, Central Finsbury) and presided over the Congress three times (1886 Calcutta, 1893 Lahore, 1906 Calcutta).

• The Surat Session (1907) is remembered for the historic split of the Congress into Moderates and Extremists.

NOTE

• The demand for "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) was adopted at the Lahore Session (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru; 26 January 1930 was celebrated as the first Independence Day.

question: Chhau, identified by the Ministry of Culture as a classical dance, is prevalent in eastern India and has three distinct forms. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marwahi Chhau of Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical dance of eastern India with three distinct styles, all named after the region of their origin:

◦ Seraikela Chhau — Jharkhand

◦ Purulia Chhau — West Bengal

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau — Odisha

• "Marwahi Chhau of Chhattisgarh" is NOT one of them — it does not exist as a recognised form of Chhau. (छऊ की तीन शैलियाँ — सरायकेला, पुरुलिया, मयूरभंज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Masks are used in the Seraikela and Purulia styles; the Mayurbhanj style is performed without masks.

• Chhau is a martial, tribal and folk-based dance and draws its themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore. It is traditionally performed during the Chaitra Parva festival.

• Chhau was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

NOTE

• Other Indian entries on UNESCO's intangible heritage list include Kutiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Ramman, Kalbelia, Mudiyettu, Sankirtana, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata and Garba of Gujarat.

question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, which of the following states is NOT included in 10 poorest states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2022, released by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), Gujarat was NOT among the ten poorest states of India. (वैश्विक बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2022)

• Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam and Odisha were among the poorest states in the report.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Global MPI measures poverty using three dimensions and ten indicators:

◦ Health — nutrition, child mortality

◦ Education — years of schooling, school attendance

◦ Standard of living — cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets

• The MPI 2022 report noted that India lifted about 415 million people out of poverty between 2005-06 and 2019-21.

• NITI Aayog publishes India's own "National Multidimensional Poverty Index" using NFHS data.

NOTE

• The MPI was developed by Sabina Alkire and James Foster (the Alkire-Foster method) at OPHI, University of Oxford, and has been part of the UNDP's Human Development Report since 2010.

question: Which Clause of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the ‘right to move freely throughout the territory of India’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clause (d).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 19(1)(d) of the Indian Constitution guarantees to all citizens the right "to move freely throughout the territory of India". (अनुच्छेद 19(1)(घ) — भारत के राज्यक्षेत्र में स्वतंत्रतापूर्वक संचरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The six freedoms under Article 19(1) are:

◦ (a) freedom of speech and expression

◦ (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms

◦ (c) to form associations or unions (or co-operative societies)

◦ (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India

◦ (e) to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India

◦ (g) to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business

• The original clause (f) — the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property — was deleted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and property became a legal right under Article 300A.

NOTE

• These freedoms are not absolute; the State may impose reasonable restrictions under Articles 19(2) to 19(6) on grounds such as sovereignty and integrity of India, public order, decency, morality, and the interests of Scheduled Tribes.

• Article 19 rights are available only to citizens, not to foreigners or companies.

question: Who among the following was a renowned player of the musical instrument called ‘Santoor’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (1938–2022) was the renowned maestro of the "Santoor", a hundred-stringed trapezoid instrument of Jammu and Kashmir. He is credited with transforming the santoor from a folk instrument into a full-fledged Indian classical concert instrument. (पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा — संतूर)

• He received the Padma Vibhushan (2001), the Padma Shri (1991) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1986).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• With flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, he formed the famous film-music duo "Shiv-Hari" (Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe, Darr).

• Option 1 Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia — Bansuri (flute); Option 2 Pandit Kumar Gandharva — celebrated Hindustani vocalist; Option 4 Pandit Ravi Shankar — Sitar.

NOTE

• The Santoor is played with a pair of light wooden mallets called "kalam". In Kashmir it is traditionally used in Sufiana Mausiqi.

• It belongs to the Tat Vadya (stringed) category of Indian musical instruments.

question: The President of India conferred the Padma Shri award to Sanathoiba Sharma for his distinguished service in the field of ______________ in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thang-Ta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanathoiba Sharma of Manipur was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for his distinguished service in the field of "Thang-Ta". (थांग-ता — मणिपुर की मार्शल आर्ट)

• "Thang-Ta" (also called Huyen Lallong) is the traditional martial art of Manipur; the name comes from "thang" (sword) and "ta" (spear).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mukna" is a traditional wrestling form of Manipur.

• Option 2 "Khong Kangjei" is a Manipuri game resembling hockey, played with the feet and a stick.

• Option 4 "Yubi Lakpi" is a Manipuri game played with a greased coconut, resembling rugby.

NOTE

• Indian martial arts: Kalaripayattu (Kerala — considered the oldest), Silambam (Tamil Nadu), Thang-Ta (Manipur), Gatka (Punjab), Mardani Khel (Maharashtra), Kalari/Thoda (Himachal Pradesh), Mallakhamb (Maharashtra/MP).

• Padma Awards are announced on Republic Day each year in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

question: Rikham pada dance belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rikham Pada" is a popular folk dance of the Nyishi (Nishi) tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It is a group dance performed by young men and women, usually on festive occasions. (रिखम पाड़ा — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh: Bardo Chham, Ponung, Wancho, Chalo, Aji Lamu, Roppi, Popir, Hiirii Khaniing.

• Major festivals of Arunachal Pradesh: Losar, Solung, Mopin, Nyokum, Dree, Si-Donyi, Boori Boot, Reh.

• Arunachal Pradesh became a full-fledged state on 20 February 1987; its capital is Itanagar.

NOTE

• Folk dances of other North-Eastern states: Assam — Bihu; Meghalaya — Nongkrem, Shad Suk Mynsiem, Laho; Mizoram — Cheraw (bamboo dance), Khuallam; Nagaland — Chang Lo/Sua Lua, Zeliang; Manipur — Thabal Chongba, Lai Haraoba; Tripura — Hojagiri, Garia; Sikkim — Singhi Chham, Maruni.

question: Which theory was published by John Dalton in 1808 to explain chemical reactions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic theory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• John Dalton published his "Atomic theory" in 1808 (in A New System of Chemical Philosophy) to explain the laws of chemical combination and chemical reactions. (डाल्टन का परमाणु सिद्धांत — 1808)

• The main postulates of Dalton's Atomic Theory are:

◦ All matter is made of tiny indivisible particles called atoms.

◦ Atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties; atoms of different elements differ.

◦ Atoms can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

◦ Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in fixed, simple whole-number ratios.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dalton's theory successfully explained the Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier), the Law of Constant/Definite Proportions (Proust) and the Law of Multiple Proportions (Dalton himself).

• Option 2 Valence bond theory — Heitler, London, Pauling and Slater; Option 3 Quantum field theory — Dirac and others; Option 4 Molecular orbital theory — Hund and Mulliken.

NOTE

• Later discoveries modified Dalton's theory: atoms are divisible (electron — J. J. Thomson, 1897; proton — Goldstein/Rutherford; neutron — James Chadwick, 1932), and isotopes show that atoms of the same element can differ in mass.

• Dalton is also known for describing colour blindness, called "Daltonism", from which he himself suffered.

question: What is the main function of money in an economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To facilitate exchange.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary/main function of money is to act as a "medium of exchange" — that is, to facilitate the exchange of goods and services by removing the difficulties of the barter system (especially the problem of the "double coincidence of wants"). (विनिमय का माध्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Functions of money are classified as:

◦ Primary functions — (i) Medium of exchange, (ii) Measure/unit of value.

◦ Secondary functions — (i) Store of value, (ii) Standard of deferred payments, (iii) Transfer of value.

◦ Contingent functions — basis of credit, distribution of national income, maximisation of satisfaction, liquidity.

• Option 1 (regulating interest rates) and Option 4 (controlling inflation) are functions of the central bank (RBI) through monetary policy, not of money itself.

• Option 2 "To create wealth" — money is a medium, not a creator of wealth by itself.

NOTE

• In India, currency notes (except the ₹1 note) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India under the RBI Act, 1934; the ₹1 note and all coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

• The RBI issues notes under the "Minimum Reserve System" (since 1957), keeping a minimum reserve of ₹200 crore (₹115 crore in gold + ₹85 crore in foreign securities).

question: Who among the following designed the India Gate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Edwin Lutyens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The India Gate in New Delhi was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, the famous British architect who planned much of New Delhi (hence "Lutyens' Delhi"). (इंडिया गेट — एडविन लुटियंस)

• Originally called the All India War Memorial, it was built to commemorate the around 84,000 Indian soldiers who died in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War. Its foundation stone was laid in 1921 by the Duke of Connaught, and it was completed/inaugurated in 1931 by Lord Irwin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker together designed New Delhi; Lutyens designed the Rashtrapati Bhavan (then Viceroy's House) and Baker designed the Secretariat (North and South Blocks) and the Parliament House (with Lutyens).

• The Amar Jawan Jyoti was added under India Gate in 1972 after the 1971 Indo-Pak war; in January 2022 its flame was merged with the flame at the National War Memorial.

• In 2022, a statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed under the India Gate canopy.

NOTE

• Options 1 and 2 (Lord Wavell, Lord Dalhousie) were British Viceroys/Governors-General, not architects. John Nash was a British architect famous for Buckingham Palace and Regent Street in London.

question: In 2022, the Centre constituted a committee headed by former Union Agriculture Secretary _______ to look into the issues of minimum support price (MSP).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Agrawal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2022, the Central Government constituted a committee headed by Sanjay Agrawal, former Union Agriculture Secretary, to look into issues relating to the Minimum Support Price (MSP), along with crop diversification and making natural farming more effective. (एमएसपी समिति — संजय अग्रवाल)

• The committee was formed following the assurance given to farmers at the time of the repeal of the three farm laws (November 2021).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is the price at which the government purchases crops from farmers to protect them from a sharp fall in market prices.

• MSP is announced by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), which was set up in 1965 and works under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

• MSP is currently announced for 22 mandated crops plus fair and remunerative price (FRP) for sugarcane.

• Option 3 Radha Mohan Singh was a former Union Agriculture Minister, not the committee head.

NOTE

• The M. S. Swaminathan Committee (National Commission on Farmers, 2004-06) recommended fixing MSP at 50% above the weighted average cost of production (C2 + 50%).

• Government procurement is carried out mainly by the Food Corporation of India (FCI), NAFED and state agencies.

question: One of the prominent festivals celebrated in ____________ is the ‘Me-Dum-Me-Phi’, i.e., the ancestor worship festival.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Me-Dam-Me-Phi" is a prominent festival of the Ahom community of Assam, celebrated on 31 January every year. It is an ancestor worship festival in which offerings are made to departed ancestors. (मे-डाम-मे-फी — असम)

• The name means "Me" (offerings), "Dam" (ancestors) and "Phi" (gods) — i.e., offering to the ancestors who have become gods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Assam: Bihu (Rongali/Bohag, Kongali/Kati and Bhogali/Magh Bihu), Ambubachi Mela (Kamakhya Temple), Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang (Mising tribe), Majuli Raas Mahotsav.

• The Ahoms ruled Assam for nearly 600 years (1228–1826); their kingdom was founded by Sukaphaa. Lachit Borphukan, the Ahom general, defeated the Mughals in the Battle of Saraighat (1671).

• Sukaphaa Divas / Asom Divas is observed on 2 December.

NOTE

• Festivals of other NE states: Nagaland — Hornbill Festival, Sekrenyi, Moatsu; Manipur — Yaoshang, Lai Haraoba, Ningol Chakouba; Meghalaya — Nongkrem, Wangala, Behdienkhlam, Shad Suk Mynsiem.

question: Which of the following is an example of revenue expenditure in the government budget?
option_3: Payment of salaries to government employees
solution_text:
The correct answer is Payment of salaries to government employees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Revenue expenditure" is expenditure that neither creates any asset nor reduces any liability of the government. The payment of salaries to government employees is a classic example — it creates no asset and reduces no liability. (राजस्व व्यय — सरकारी कर्मचारियों के वेतन का भुगतान)

• Other examples of revenue expenditure: interest payments, subsidies, pensions, grants, defence revenue expenditure, expenditure on the maintenance of assets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Capital expenditure" creates assets or reduces liabilities:

◦ Option 1 "Construction of a new highway" → creates an asset ⇒ capital expenditure.

◦ Option 2 "Investment in a State-owned company" → creates a financial asset ⇒ capital expenditure.

◦ Option 4 "Repayment of a loan" → reduces a liability ⇒ capital expenditure.

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings).

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement"; since 2017 it is presented on 1 February, and the separate Railway Budget was merged with it in the same year.

• The FRBM Act, 2003 aims to institutionalise fiscal discipline and reduce the fiscal deficit.

question: ‘The Fall of a Sparrow’ is an autobiography of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salim Ali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Fall of a Sparrow" (1985) is the autobiography of Dr. Salim Ali, the celebrated Indian ornithologist known as the "Birdman of India". (सलीम अली की आत्मकथा)

• The title refers to the incident in his childhood when he shot a sparrow with a toy air-gun and became curious about its unusual yellow throat — an event that started his lifelong interest in birds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dr. Salim Moizuddin Abdul Ali (1896–1987) wrote "The Book of Indian Birds" and conducted systematic bird surveys across India. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1958) and the Padma Vibhushan (1976).

• He played a key role in the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) and in saving the Bharatpur (Keoladeo) Bird Sanctuary and the Silent Valley forests.

• National Bird Watching Day / Salim Ali's birth anniversary is observed on 12 November.

• The Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is in Goa; the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON) is at Coimbatore.

NOTE

• Other autobiographies: Raj Kapoor — subject of the biography Raj Kapoor: The Master at Work; Kapil Dev — Straight from the Heart; Atal Bihari Vajpayee — Meri Ikyavan Kavitayen (poetry collection, not an autobiography).
